title: Whole net-contribution arguments with reported-opinion and reward scope

source.witness_limit: 1857 printed witness, not a newly checked medieval manuscript.

complete_content_inventory: Two men bring3 and2 loaves; they go to a fountain and sit to eat.
They invite a passing soldier, who joins them; all five loaves are eaten by the three.
The departing soldier leaves5 bezants as a courtesy.
Initial recipients take3 and2 coins according to their3 and2 loaves; ask whether this division is right.
The source reports the view that one coin per loaf makes this right, then explicitly calls that view false.
It argues that all three ate the five loaves, so each received1+2/3 loaves.
It then apportions what the soldier ate between the original owners and concludes rewards4 and1; the owned table repeats4 and1.
The fountain, invitation, departure, courtesy, reported opinion and rejection belong to the whole account; they are not arithmetic padding.
design.fraction_collation_limit: The smaller stacked fractions in the intermediate attribution sentence remain a diplomatic-reading caveat. The source has a mixed-number expression and a following fraction that appears to read4/5, with denominator ownership requiring careful collation. This card does not silently transcribe those marks as4/3 or4/9. The derived net quantities4/3 and1/3 below are explicitly modern arithmetic from the clearly read setup/equal shares; the source final4/1 and table are clear.

explicit_assumptions: Equal loaf units/value in the mathematical account
Equal individual consumption is the source explanation, not inferred from generic eating alone
Reward proportional to net bread supplied to guest is the source problem convention, not a universal rule of fairness
Owners consume their own entitled portions before net guest contributions are computed; this is an allocation account, not observed bite-by-bite provenance

design.concrete_contrast: Gross-contribution allocation also conserves the5 coins and gives3/2, but violates the net-supply ratio. Thus total conservation and repeated numerals do not distinguish the readings; participant roles, own consumption and the scope of the rejected opinion jointly do. Treating both quoted division claims as endorsed would create a false contradiction.
symmetries_and_failure: Globally renaming the two owners changes no structure.
Bread and money units can rescale independently until a rate/unit relation is bound.
If consumption differs, donors exchange their own shares, or reward follows another convention,4/1 is not entailed; these are substantive rival assumptions.
Free redistribution of bread provenance or freely labeling a statement as quoted/false would make every account satisfiable and is disallowed.
No target reward/ownership case is independently identified; this may be only an arithmetic tale unrelated to the manuscript.
design.closest_predecessors: IDEA350 concerns graded alloy composition and source recipes, IDEA360 fixed-participant subset totals and solvability status, IDEA358 rational reduction. This adds net contribution after self-consumption and explicit reported-opinion scope. It does not rerun their numerical writers or claim global conservation is novel. W94 identity-assumption stop remains applicable; its primary was read in the earlier bounded task.
design.data_needed: A complete-passage ownership hypothesis, a finite common grammar distinguishing possession/consumption/transfer/payment and reported versus endorsed assertions, globally shared numerals if used, and an independent rival/owner. No exact copied source length is a target prediction.
